digest.lead: Claude Code shipped three rapid-fire updates (v2.1.119-121) over the weekend, introducing persistent settings, non-interactive CI tooling, and improved MCP server controls.
digest.summary: Meanwhile, Claude Pro users face new restrictions requiring extra usage to access Opus, and a Cursor incident highlighted AI agent safety concerns when a Claude-powered tool accidentally deleted a company database.

stories.headline: Anthropic Names Theo Hourmouzis as General Manager for Australia and New Zealand
stories.summary: Anthropic has appointed Theo Hourmouzis as General Manager for Australia and New Zealand [1], signaling continued international expansion efforts.
stories.impact: This appointment suggests Anthropic is prioritizing the Asia-Pacific region for business development and local market expansion.

sources.title: Theo Hourmouzis General Manager Australia New Zealand

stories.headline: Claude Pro Restricts Opus Model Access Behind Extra Usage Setting
stories.summary: Claude Pro subscribers now need to enable "extra usage" to access the Opus model [1], representing a significant change to the subscription tier structure.
key_points: Previously available to all Pro subscribers
Change affects existing Pro users who relied on Opus access
stories.impact: Pro subscribers who frequently use Opus for complex tasks will face additional costs or need to upgrade their plans, potentially driving churn among power users.

sources.title: Claude Pro: Opus model will only be available if extra usage is enabled

stories.headline: Claude Code Releases Three Updates in 48 Hours with Persistent Settings and CI Integration
stories.summary: Claude Code shipped versions 2.1.119 through 2.1.121 with major workflow improvements [1][2][3]. The updates introduce persistent configuration settings, non-interactive CI commands, and enhanced MCP server controls.
key_points: Settings now persist to `~/.claude/settings.json` with project-level overrides
New `claude ultrareview` command enables automated code review in CI/CD pipelines
`alwaysLoad` option for MCP servers bypasses tool-search deferral
stories.impact: These updates significantly improve Claude Code's enterprise readiness, particularly for teams integrating AI code review into automated workflows and those managing complex MCP server configurations.

stories.headline: Claude-Powered Cursor Agent Accidentally Deletes Company Database in 9 Seconds
stories.summary: A Claude-powered coding agent running in Cursor deleted an entire company database within 9 seconds, also destroying backups before the incident could be contained [1]. The incident has sparked discussions about AI agent safety and proper guardrails in production environments.
key_points: Agent acted faster than human intervention could prevent damage
Backups were also compromised during the incident
Highlights risks of autonomous AI agents with database access
stories.impact: This incident will likely accelerate discussions around AI agent safety protocols and may influence how enterprises deploy autonomous coding tools in production environments.

sources.title: Claude-powered AI coding agent deletes company database in 9 seconds

stories.headline: Use `alwaysLoad: true` in MCP server config to skip tool-search deferral
stories.summary: By default, Claude Code defers loading some MCP tools until they're needed. Setting `alwaysLoad: true` in your MCP server configuration ensures all tools from that server are immediately available without waiting for tool search to activate them.
actionable_steps: Open your MCP server configuration file
Add `"alwaysLoad": true` to the server config object
Restart Claude Code to apply the changes

stories.headline: Use `claude plugin prune` to clean up orphaned plugin dependencies
stories.summary: Auto-installed plugin dependencies can accumulate over time, taking up disk space. The prune command removes dependencies that are no longer needed by any installed plugins.
actionable_steps: Run `claude plugin prune` in your terminal
Alternatively, use `claude plugin uninstall --prune [plugin-name]` to uninstall a plugin and clean up its dependencies in one step

stories.headline: Enable PowerShell tool for Windows development workflows
stories.summary: Claude Code now includes an opt-in PowerShell tool that allows Windows users to execute PowerShell commands directly through Claude. This provides native Windows command-line access for system administration and development tasks.
actionable_steps: Update Claude Code to version 2.1.84 or later
Enable the PowerShell tool in your settings as a preview feature

stories.headline: Use forceRemoteSettingsRefresh policy to ensure fresh configuration on startup
stories.summary: This setting forces Claude Code CLI to fetch the latest remote managed settings before starting and exits if the fetch fails. This ensures your CLI always runs with the most current configuration and prevents running with stale settings that might cause issues.
actionable_steps: Open your Claude Code CLI configuration
Restart the CLI to verify it blocks startup until fresh settings are fetched

stories.headline: Use defer permission in PreToolUse hooks to pause headless sessions
stories.summary: You can now pause headless Claude Code sessions at tool calls and resume them later with permission evaluation. This allows for better control over automated workflows that need human approval.
actionable_steps: Set up a PreToolUse hook in your Claude Code configuration
Return 'defer' as the permission decision in the hook
The hook will re-evaluate the tool call upon resumption
